# Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI

**Company:** Quillstone Payments (fictional name; card-payment and business-tools provider)
**Location:** Hamburg, Germany (office-first)
**Team:** AI team within Customer Operations

## About the team

The Customer Operations organisation wants merchants to get help quickly and without friction. The AI team builds models and assistants that answer merchant questions, route tickets and help support agents. You will work with backend engineers, data scientists and product managers to take ideas from prototype to production.

## What you will do

- Build, deploy and operate AI and machine learning systems used by the support organisation
- Maintain pipelines for data processing, training and serving
- Fine-tune and evaluate models, including language models, for accuracy and cost
- Prepare and clean large text datasets
- Apply normal engineering discipline: version control, CI/CD and automated tests
- Integrate ML components into the wider product with other engineering teams

## Requirements

- Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
- At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
- Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
- Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
- Strong Python; familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
- Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines

## Benefits

- Annual learning budget, employee share programme and company pension contribution
- Relocation support and subsidised meals
- Sabbatical after several years of service

company_info.company_description:
Quillstone Payments is a privately held financial-services company founded in 2013 and headquartered in Hamburg. It builds payment and money-management tools for small merchants, including card terminals, a point-of-sale app and a business account, and has recently added a personal account for merchants’ customers. The company serves millions of merchants across Europe and the Americas and employs around 2,500 people in roughly 20 offices. Its teams span product, engineering and operations, with machine-learning work focused on customer-support automation and fraud detection.

Quillstone emphasizes ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes. Teams have autonomy to solve merchants’ problems, with shared values and open communication preferred over heavy processes. The culture values pragmatism, humility, candid feedback and sharing context. It is office-first, with some flexible days agreed by teams, and supports development through training budgets, peer feedback, internal tech talks and twice-yearly development-plan reviews. The company also supports local business education projects and publishes an annual inclusion report.

- Weekly forecast of orders per recipe and region, 6 weeks ahead; LightGBM with calendar, price and menu-position features.
- Runs as a scheduled notebook job (Vertex AI Workbench scheduled notebook) writing to BigQuery; operations reads it in Looker.
- WAPE 23% -> 14%; estimated food waste reduction of 9%.
- Technologies: Python, LightGBM, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker.

PROJECT: Sequential A/B Testing Calculator (Thistlebox, 2023)
- Streamlit app for planning and analysing experiments with sequential boundaries; used by ~25 people in product and growth.
- Hosted by the data platform team on Cloud Run; I wrote the app and the Dockerfile, they handle deployment.
- Technologies: Python, Streamlit, statsmodels, Docker.

PROJECT: Churn Propensity and Retention Targeting (Thistlebox, 2024-2025)
- XGBoost churn model scored weekly in BigQuery; retention offers sent to top-decile customers.
- Validated with a 10% holdout: churn down 2.1 percentage points in the treated group.
- Technologies: Python, XGBoost, SHAP, BigQuery, dbt.

PROJECT: Image classification course project (personal, 2025)
- Followed an online deep learning course and fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food images dataset (~80% accuracy). Learning project only.
- Technologies: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

EXPERIENCE: Data Scientist at Thistlebox (2022-Present)
- Experimentation, forecasting, churn modelling.

EXPERIENCE: Junior Data Analyst at Firth Energy Retail (2020-2022)
- Segmentation, R Markdown regulatory reports.
